newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE WHEAT MAKES SLIGHT GAIN DESPITE RAIN.
newsitem.headline: SFE WHEAT MAKES SLIGHT GAIN DESPITE RAIN.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures rose slightly on Thursday despite reasonable rainfall in the past 24 hours.
Prices opened weaker on overnight rain of about 10 mm in Australia's drought-affected eastern and southern wheatbelt.
But futures prices recovered during the morning to end up by about A$1.00 a tonne as the rain was assessed to have saved the crop from further deterioration, but was lighter than had been hoped for.
January 1998 was the only futures contract to trade, rising by A$1.00 to A$199.50 on nine lots. Settlement prices of untraded contracts generally rose by about A$1.00 a tonne.
Ten January 1998 put options were taken out at a strike price of A$195.00 as a hedge.

Gary Booth of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said that a record volume of more than 100 options traded by Ords on the SYCOM system on Friday night highlighted strong interest by growers in options in the current market.
The market was "absolutely weather dominated". Rain had stopped crop deterioration but more rain was needed, he said.
